fields.Front: State the three semantic guidelines for drawing an ER diagram, and say which is strict in this course.
fields.Back:
1. Entity names all SINGULAR (her preference, and required in this course) or all plural - never mixed.
2. MEANINGFUL names for entities, attributes and relationships - 'don't use like item one or object two'.
3. Relationships should read LEFT TO RIGHT and TOP TO BOTTOM; rename the verb or swap the entities' positions. This one is not always possible - 'it's not a big deal if you can't' - but singular names are required.

fields.Front: What are the three things wrong with PATIENT --- Treats --- DOCTORS --- Is employee by --- NURSE?
fields.Back:
1. 'Patient treats doctor' reads backwards: rename it IS TREATED BY, or swap DOCTOR and PATIENT.
2. 'Doctors' is plural while Patient and Nurse are singular: make it DOCTOR.
3. 'Doctor is employed by nurse' is backwards and ungrammatical top to bottom: it should be Doctor EMPLOYS Nurse.

fields.Front: What cardinality and participation does the instructor give the doctor's-office example?
fields.Back: Patient IS TREATED BY Doctor: MANY-TO-MANY (a patient may see many doctors, and a doctor 'for sure' treats many), both total - every patient we track has a doctor and every doctor treats someone. Doctor EMPLOYS Nurse: ONE-TO-MANY, both total, one doctor per nurse 'assuming a single doctor's office'. She warns she has not given enough information to be sure.

fields.Text: In the case study 'Department works for employee' reads badly, so the relationship is renamed {{c1::has}} (department has employee); the one visual fault she fixes is a {{c1::line cutting through an attribute}} - some overlap is fine, lines through ovals are not.

Textbook (Elmasri §3.7.3): design refinements - an attribute that turns out to reference another entity type is refined into {{c1::a relationship}} (and the attribute is then deleted); an attribute appearing in several entity types may be {{c1::promoted to an entity type}} of its own; and an entity type with a single attribute related to only one other type may be {{c1::demoted to an attribute}}.
